captions.caption: Fig. 1. Device layout. A wax delay bridge of length L is printed across a 2 mm cellulose channel between the inlet and the detection zone and heated at 120 °C for 60 s.

captions.label: Fig. 2
captions.caption: Fig. 2. Delay time against bridge length. Points: mean ± standard deviation of five devices; dashed line: quadratic fit t = k·L² with k = 24.6 s/mm².

captions.label: Fig. 3
captions.caption: Fig. 3. Coefficient of variation of the delay for each bridge length, with the value reported for sugar barriers in ref. [3] (grey). Dotted line: 15 %.

captions.label: Table 1
captions.caption: Table 1. Timing elements for paper microfluidics. Wax delay bridge: delay 42-612 s, variation 9-13 %, no added material. Sugar barrier [3]: delay 60-900 s, variation about 25 %, added sugar layer. Mechanical valve [2]: delay set by the user, variation below 5 %, added parts and assembly.
